title: Masayoshi Son Admits Mistake: Not Investing in Anthropic Was a Huge Mistake, I Really Wish I Had Invested at the Time

content_html:
Nikkei Asia reported that SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son openly admitted at an event in Tokyo on Wednesday that missing out on investing in Anthropic early on was one of the "mistakes" he had made. "When I met Dario Amodei in person, I thought he was truly remarkable, and I really wish I had invested then." It wasn't that SoftBank hadn't considered it; it had already committed to backing OpenAI and had begun spending heavily, and his explanation was that he couldn't "chase two rabbits at once."

He was also clear about the strategic contradiction: spreading bets across several companies is usually safer, but to form a true partnership, you have to place a heavy bet on one—"You have to give more weight to certain investments, otherwise you cannot truly become a partner." As he spoke, Anthropic was preparing to go public this week.

Son also pushed back on the claim that the AI boom has turned into a bubble: "Artificial intelligence has only just begun; those who call it a bubble have completely missed the point." He recalled that after the dot-com bubble burst in 2000, SoftBank stopped investing because it lacked money, and this time he was glad to have room to maneuver. He also defended an investment-led model: the goal is not to make money through investment, but to create the future through investment.

Although he had invested in OpenAI, he stressed that chips and data centers should also serve other AI developers, including Anthropic—"If you only support OpenAI, you cannot become a platform." Finally, he zoomed out: no longer fixating on short-term returns and share prices, "the real show has only just begun."
